Paragraph: "Well mingled are these female birds with their male ones, for which they are well admired by their own flock, oh! Soumitri, and such birds are calling gladsomely together with the pleasing humming of king-bees...
Situation/Problem_Faced: Observing bird couples rejoicing in companionship makes Rama acutely conscious of his own solitude.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Rama points out the natural union and harmony among paired birds and bees.
Outcome/Resolution: The sight emphasizes his painful separation from Seetha.
Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Pairing in nature (Mithuna) reflects the cosmic balance of divine forces, making its absence in Rama's life stand out sharply.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Social comparison: witnessing harmonious partnerships in nature intensifies subjective distress over one's lost relationship.
